TEXT
The brain drain is one of the biggest challenges facing developing countries today. Every year, thousands of talented doctors, engineers and scientists leave their home countries to work in richer nations, where salaries are higher and working conditions are better. For the individuals, this migration is often a rational choice: they seek a better life and more opportunities. However, for their home countries, the loss is enormous. These nations have spent years and money educating their best minds, only to see them enrich other economies. Hospitals lack doctors, universities lose their best professors, and development slows down. To reverse this trend, governments must create attractive opportunities at home: better salaries, modern equipment and real chances for research and promotion. A country that values its talents will keep them.

I. READING COMPREHENSION (8 marks)
1) What does the expression "brain drain" refer to?   (2 marks)
2) Why do talented people leave their home countries?   (2 marks)
3) Why is the brain drain a great loss for developing countries?   (2 marks)
4) What must governments do to reverse this trend?   (2 marks)

II. LANGUAGE (6 marks)
1) Complete with "must": Governments ______ create attractive opportunities at home.   (1,5 marks)
2) Put into the passive: "These nations have educated their best minds."   (2 marks)
3) Complete with a relative pronoun (who / which): A country ______ values its talents will keep them.   (1,5 marks)
4) Give the opposite of "leave" = ______.   (1 mark)

III. WRITING (6 marks)
"How can developing countries stop the brain drain?" Write a composition (about 12 lines) proposing solutions, with arguments. Use "should / must" and linkers.
